definition: the use of irony to mock or convey contempt
hook: Sarcasm is supposed to be funny. Its Greek roots are not.
modernAnchor: Oh great, another Monday. Thanks for your help. The words say one thing. They mean another.

origin.originalMeaning: to tear flesh, to bite the lips in rage

journey: The Greek sarx meant flesh. Sarkazein meant to strip it away - like an animal at a bone.
Greek writers used it to describe cutting speech - the kind of words that left marks.
Latin took the word. Scholars carried it into French. By the 1500s it arrived in English.
Three thousand years of violent imagery compressed into a tone of voice you use at the office.
